html:
The Jim Crow laws were state and local laws in the American South that enforced the separation of Black and white people and kept Black citizens from voting, after the end of Reconstruction in 1877.

Schools, trains, buses, hospitals and even cemeteries were segregated. Poll taxes, literacy tests and white primaries stripped most Black men of the vote. In Plessy v. Ferguson (1896) the Supreme Court approved "separate but equal". Lynching enforced the system by terror.

Millions of Black Southerners left for the North in the Great Migration. The civil rights movement wore Jim Crow down through Brown v. Board of Education in 1954, the Montgomery bus boycott and the Civil Rights Act of 1964, with the Voting Rights Act of 1965.
sum: The Jim Crow laws were state and local laws in the American South that enforced the separation of Black and white people and kept Black citizens from voting, after the end of Reconstruction in 1877.
